newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow blast kills businessman, injures bodyguards.
newsitem.headline: Moscow blast kills businessman, injures bodyguards.

text.p: A bomb explosion killed the head of a commercial firm and wounded his two bodyguards in what Interfax news agency said could be a new twist in the battle for influence in Russia's cut-throat business world.

Interfax quoted police and interior ministry sources as saying Gennady Dzen, chief executive of the Roskontraktpostavka trading firm, was killed as he left his Jeep-style car and was about to enter his office in Mantulinskaya Street, not far from the White House government building.
It said Dzen was carrying documents indicating he was an aide to ultra-nationalist parliamentarian Vladimir Zhirinovsky.
Interfax said police were considering several possibilities, including that there had been "a financial-criminal settling of accounts".
A Reuters Television crew said the explosion, in a courtyard enclosed by a police station, an army recruiting station and commercial offices, broke windows in several buildings up to the fifth floor.
Police on the spot said the bomb, equivalent to 500 gramms of TNT, could have been planted in a water drainage pipe next to the doorway.
Interfax quoted police sources as saying the explosion had been caused by a radio-controlled device.
Bombings by mafia-style groups and armed show-downs have become a frequent occurrence in the new Russia's business world.
